newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland readies bill to fight money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Poland readies bill to fight money laundering.

text.p: The Polish government is preparing a new law to combat money laundering, interior minister Leszek Miller said on Tuesday.
"The finance minister, with my help, is readying a draft law with new measures against money laundering," Miller told a news conference. He said it was too early to give details.

Money laundering -- disguising the origins of earnings from criminal sources such as drug and arms trafficking or prostitution -- appeared in Poland after the 1989 fall of communism when the country liberalised its banking system. @
Criminal groups usually use intermediary firms to inject cash into the financial system to make it appear to have come from legitimate sources.
In 1995, the then Prime Minister Jozef Oleksy estimated crime groups had legalised some $3 billion in Poland in the several previous years.

Poland has since introduced many measures against money laundering and other organised crime, including police powers to mount "sting" operations against gangsters, allowing undercover police to offer bribes or buy drugs and infiltrate criminal groups. @
It has also eased banking secrecy rules, giving tax inspectors more access to personal and company banking accounts and transfers.
